# Temple Scroll Column 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 4 | **Condition:** Heavily damaged; Passover/Unleavened Bread regulations

---

**4:1** [...] you-shall-offer [...] a-burnt-offering to-the-LORD [...]

**4:2** [...] two young-bulls and-one ram [...]

**4:3** [...] and-seven he-lambs sons-of-a-year without-blemish [...]

**4:4** [...] and-one he-goat for-a-sin-offering [...]

**4:5** [...] to-make-atonement for-you [...]

**4:6** [...] and-their-grain-offerings [...] fine-flour mixed with-oil [...]

**4:7** [...] three-tenths for-the-bull and-two-tenths for-the-ram [...]

**4:8** [...] and-one-tenth for-the-one lamb [...]

**4:9** [...] and-wine for-their-drink-offerings [...]

**4:10** [...] thus you-shall-do for-each day of-the-seven days [...]

**4:11** [...] and-you-shall-count [...] seven complete weeks [...]

**4:12** [...] from-the-day of-your-bringing the-sheaf of-the-wave-offering [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 4 continues the Passover and Unleavened Bread regulations, specifying the daily burnt offerings (cf. Num 28:19-24). The sacrificial roster — two bulls, one ram, seven yearling lambs, one goat for purification — closely follows the Pentateuchal prescriptions. The grain offering measures (three-tenths, two-tenths, one-tenth of an ephah) are standard. Lines 11-12 transition to the counting toward the Festival of Weeks (cf. Lev 23:15-16).*
